analysis.title: CIO Update: Stay the course
key_insights: The bank keeps its overweight allocation to equities despite higher volatility. It cites strong growth and robust corporate earnings.
The US economy is solid, supported by AI-related capital expenditure, consumer spending and a strong labour market. The investment boom is spreading from technology to manufacturing.
Persistently high core inflation and rising energy prices lead the bank to conclude US monetary policy is not restrictive enough. It expects a Fed hike to 4.25% in December and further hikes in 2027.
The bank expects the ECB to raise its deposit rate to 2.75% in December, with another hike in early 2027, driven by energy-led inflation. The euro area is more resilient than expected.

France is a growing concern. Political instability and no credible fiscal consolidation plan are pushing borrowing costs to new highs. The French-German 10-year spread is about 150 basis points, and French credit spreads are likely to widen while it is unclear where the ECB would intervene.
The SNB is expected to raise its policy rate to 0.5% in the first half of 2027. The UK faces modest growth with persistent inflation, and the bank sees some more tightening in the coming months.

Japan benefits from exports, rising real wages and fiscal measures, with a weak yen supporting exporters. Renewed inflation pressure points to further tightening. China is mixed, with strong exports, weak domestic demand and a weak property sector.

Bonds: the bank favours medium-term government bonds for carry and roll-down. Corporate credit spreads have widened from very tight levels, and high-yield and AT1 bonds look reasonably valued if the economy stays robust.

Equities: global markets made no further gains in October. US equities held up relatively well despite tech weakness, energy benefited from higher oil, and financials underperformed. The bank prefers developed over emerging markets, with the US and Switzerland favoured, and expects rotation from cyclicals to defensives such as staples and healthcare.

Valuations have fallen below the 10-year average in the US and Europe because earnings grew while prices were flat or lower. Sentiment has deteriorated and investors have cut risk, which the bank says sets up a possible year-end rally.
Asset allocation: equities stay overweight, bonds slightly underweight. The bank trimmed emerging-market government bonds and added high-yield bonds. Gold and commodities remain neutral.
The bank says a more defensive positioning may be appropriate for 2027 given high oil prices, tighter financing conditions and fiscal uncertainty.

earnings_insights: Corporate earnings growth is described as strong and above average, but the report gives no company-specific figures. Earnings growth with flat or lower prices pushed US and European valuations below their 10-year average.

Volatility in government bond markets has increased on the reassessment of the policy outlook and public finances.

France faces political instability ahead of the 2027 presidential elections, which limits fiscal consolidation and weighs on the euro.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong growth, AI investment, robust earnings and valuations below the 10-year average support equities, with deteriorated sentiment setting up a year-end rally.
tension_points.bear_case: High oil prices, tighter financing conditions, fiscal uncertainty, higher discount rates and AI bubble fears may call for more defensive positioning in 2027.
